7.1 Detailed Breakdown of the SQL Layer and Database ER Diagram (sql/)

The Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram below shows the three tables inside the database (PAYMENT_LEDGER, AGENT_TRIAGE_OUTBOX, and FRAUD_SIGNATURES), every column and data type, which columns are accelerated by the AlloyDB Columnar Engine and alloydb_scann, and how they connect during the self-immunizing loop:

  1. sql/01_schema.sql: The Three Core Tables payment_ledger: Stores every instant transfer (tx_id UUID PRIMARY KEY, sender_account_id, receiver_account_id, device_fingerprint, merchant_category, selectivity_bucket, amount_cents, tx_timestamp, behavioral_vec vector(64), composite_risk_score, and decision). fraud_signatures: Stores confirmed 64-D fraud patterns (signature_id UUID PRIMARY KEY, merchant_category, selectivity_bucket, created_at, source in 'SEED_CORPUS' | 'CHURN_STREAM' | 'GEMINI_AGENT_IMMUNIZED', behavioral_vec vector(64), and pattern_description). agent_triage_outbox: Stores suspicious grey-zone payments (outbox_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, tx_id with ON DELETE CASCADE, status in 'PENDING' | 'PROCESSING' | 'COMPLETED' | 'FAILED', lease_token UUID for fencing stale workers, payload JSONB, agent_verdict, agent_rationale, created_at, and processed_at) along with a partial index idx_outbox_pending_poll (WHERE status IN ('PENDING', 'PROCESSING')) so background workers find pending items and recover stalled leases in sub-millisecond time.
  2. sql/02_setup_alloydb.sql: AlloyDB Columnar Engine and alloydb_scann Setup Loads alloydb_scann, google_columnar_engine, and google_ml_integration. Creates the shared B-Tree indexes (idx_ledger_velocity_btree, idx_ledger_sender_24h, and idx_fraud_sig_filters) and builds idx_fraud_sig_scann: CREATE INDEX idx_fraud_sig_scann ON fraud_signatures USING scann (behavioral_vec cosine) WITH (num_leaves = 100, quantizer = 'sq8');. Configures 8 database-level SCaNN parameters via ALTER DATABASE postgres SET (including scann.vector_node_min_dimensionality = 32, scann.custom_scan_replace_prefilter = on, scann.num_leaves_to_search = 15, and scann.pre_reordering_num_neighbors = 50) to enable single-stage bitmap pre-filtering (Custom Scan (vector scan)), and calls SELECT google_columnar_engine_add('public.payment_ledger', ...) to pin the analytical columns in the SIMD columnar cache.
  3. sql/03_setup_aurora_baseline.sql: Fair AWS Aurora Baseline Creates the identical relational B-Tree indexes (idx_ledger_velocity_btree and idx_ledger_sender_24h) on payment_ledger, drops idx_fraud_sig_filters (DROP INDEX IF EXISTS) so Aurora evaluates true HNSW post-filtering, and builds the pgvector HNSW index (USING hnsw (behavioral_vec vector_cosine_ops) WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64)) on fraud_signatures.
  4. sql/queries/hot_path_authorize.sql: Inside the 5-Stage Single-Trip CTE Stage 1 (corridor_stats + sender_velocity -> velocity_window): Separates the 24-hour corridor average (corridor_stats using now() - INTERVAL '24 hours' for pure SIMD Columnar Engine aggregate pushdown) from the sender's individual 24-hour velocity (sender_velocity using Index Only Scan on idx_ledger_sender_24h for sum_24h_cents, tx_count_24h, and distinct_devices_24h). Stage 2 (vector_anomaly): Queries fraud_signatures with WHERE merchant_category = $3 AND selectivity_bucket <= $4 ORDER BY behavioral_vec <=> $2::vector(64) LIMIT 10, converting cosine distance into similarity 1.0 - distance. Stage 3 (risk_eval): Computes composite_score using the weighted formula (35% 24h velocity + 15% device churn + 50% vector similarity) plus the circuit-breaker override: if max_vec_sim >= 0.92, GREATEST(...) immediately elevates the score to max_vec_sim (>= 0.92), guaranteeing that any transaction matching a known fraud signature is blocked even if the account has zero prior spending today. Stage 4 (inserted_tx): Inserts the transfer into payment_ledger with decision = 'BLOCKED' (>= 0.85), 'FLAGGED_GREY_ZONE' (0.60..0.8499), or 'APPROVED' (< 0.60). Stage 5 (outbox_enqueue): Conditionally inserts a 12-field JSONB forensic payload into agent_triage_outbox when decision = 'FLAGGED_GREY_ZONE', returning (tx_id, composite_risk_score, decision, outbox_id) to the caller in one atomic transaction.

7.2 Detailed Breakdown of the Python Classes (src/)

  1. src/benchmark/feature_generator.py: Synthetic Traffic, UUIDv7, and 64-D Vector Math UUIDv7Generator: Generates time-ordered 128-bit UUIDs (RFC 9562 UUIDv7) where the first 48 bits store the Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Unlike random UUIDv4 keys that scatter writes across random disk pages and fragment B-Tree indexes, UUIDv7 keys append sequentially at the right edge of the B-Tree. BehavioralVectorProjector: Deterministically maps a TransactionContext into a 64-dimensional numpy.float64 vector (list[float]) normalized to unit length (||v||_2 = 1.0). It also provides perturb(base_vec, target_cosine_similarity) (exposed on the facade as create_perturbed_vector) to simulate fraud rings mutating their scripts to an exact cosine similarity around known attack centroids. RiskScoringPolicy: Encapsulates the composite risk formula and decision thresholds (APPROVED, FLAGGED_GREY_ZONE, BLOCKED), mirrored against the SQL CTE and verified by unit tests in tests/unit/test_risk_scoring_math.py. PaymentWorkloadGenerator: Orchestrates synthetic PIX/FedNow payment requests (generate_payment_request), normal and anomalous behavioral contexts (generate_random_context), and SQL parameter binding (bind_hot_path_sql and PaymentRequest.to_sql_params).
  2. src/benchmark/seeder.py: High-Speed Bulk Seeding and Engine Strategy Pattern EngineInitializerStrategy (Abstract Base Class): Defines how each database engine configures its extensions and indexes after bulk data is loaded: AlloyDBEngineInitializer: Selected via --engine-mode alloydb; executes sql/02_setup_alloydb.sql (enabling the Columnar Engine and building the alloydb_scann index), with automatic fallback to sql/03_setup_aurora_baseline.sql when run against standard PostgreSQL. AuroraBaselineEngineInitializer: Selected via --engine-mode aurora; executes sql/03_setup_aurora_baseline.sql. DatabaseSeeder: Streams millions of ledger rows and fraud signatures directly into PostgreSQL memory using cursor.copy("COPY ... FROM STDIN") in 25,000-row batches, runs ANALYZE so the query planner and SCaNN k-means quantizer have fresh statistics, and invokes the chosen EngineInitializerStrategy.
  3. src/benchmark/runner.py: Asynchronous 500 TPS Runner and Plan/Recall Evaluators DatabaseStatsCollector and DatabaseBlockCounters: Query pg_stat_database before and after the timed run to compute the exact shared_buffer_hit_ratio delta. ExplainPlanAnalyzer: Executes EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) outside the timed loop and inspects the JSON plan tree to confirm Custom Scan (Columnar Scan) and idx_fraud_sig_scann vs. idx_fraud_sig_hnsw. RecallEvaluator: Measures Recall@10 across probe vectors per selectivity bucket (500, 50, 5) by comparing index results against exact brute-force ground truth (SET LOCAL enable_indexscan = off; SET LOCAL enable_bitmapscan = off;). HTAPBenchmarkRunner: Before every columnar run, executes VACUUM payment_ledger and google_columnar_engine_refresh('public.payment_ledger'); uses psycopg_pool.AsyncConnectionPool to sustain 500 TPS (90% hot_path_authorize.sql executions + 10% fraud_signatures churn inserts with source = 'CHURN_STREAM'), measures Recall@10 with num_probes = 15, and records p50, p95, and p99 latencies into a validated BenchmarkResult Pydantic model.
  4. src/agent/triage_worker.py: Three-Phase Lock-Free Autonomous Agent OutboxRepository: Handles all SQL operations on agent_triage_outbox and fraud_signatures (reclaim_stale_leases, claim_pending_batch, and complete_triage_and_immunize). FraudInferenceStrategy (Strategy Pattern, where each class provides a swappable way to call the AI): InDatabaseVertexAIStrategy: Calls Gemini 4 Hydrogen from inside AlloyDB using SELECT google_ml.predict_row(model_id => 'gemini-4-hydrogen', ...). GenAISDKStrategy: Calls Gemini 4 Hydrogen (gemini-4-hydrogen) via the google-genai Python SDK with response_mime_type="application/json" and validates the response via AgentAssessment. DeterministicLocalStrategy: Evaluates payloads locally without cloud credentials for offline testing and continuous integration (and automatically serves as a safe fallback if a remote AI call fails). AgentTriageWorker.process_once: Executes the three-phase cycle: Phase 1 (Claim): Reclaims stale leases older than 30 seconds (clearing lease_token), claims a batch of PENDING rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, sets status = 'PROCESSING' and lease_token = gen_random_uuid(), and commits immediately (< 2 ms) so no row locks are held during AI inference. Phase 2 (Infer): Runs FraudInferenceStrategy.evaluate completely outside any database transaction (~3.5 s live measured on Vertex AI gemini-4-hydrogen). Phase 3 (Immunize): Calls complete_triage_and_immunize to execute a fenced UPDATE (AND status = 'PROCESSING' AND lease_token = $2::UUID) marking the outbox row 'COMPLETED' (aborting if rowcount == 0 to block zombie overwrites) and, when verdict == 'CONFIRMED_FRAUD' and confidence_score >= 0.85, inserts the 64-D vector into fraud_signatures (source = 'GEMINI_AGENT_IMMUNIZED') with the >= 0.98 cosine deduplication check.
  5. src/benchmark/reporter.py: Telemetry Aggregator and Markdown/CSV Exporter CsvTelemetryExporter and MarkdownReportFormatter: Aggregate the telemetry JSON files (--inputs) and generate results/benchmark_summary.md and results/raw_telemetry.csv.
There Are No Dumb Questions Q: Why does the code use UUIDv7 instead of the famous UUIDv4 to give every payment an ID? A: UUIDv4 is 100% random — it's like shoving new sheets into random pages of a binder, constantly splitting and scrambling the B-Tree index! UUIDv7 starts with the exact millisecond timestamp, so every new payment appends neatly at the end of the binder — much faster to write and search.
